evals.prompt: I need to fix a single failing test in one Go file — no other files are involved, and there's no written spec or RFC for this. A colleague suggests setting up a full RFC-driven multi-agent DAG with a merge queue for this. Is that the right pattern? What would you use instead and why?
evals.expected_output: Recommends against the DAG pattern for a single-file, single-unit change and suggests a simple sequential pipeline instead, since the coordination overhead of a DAG only pays off with genuinely interdependent parallel work.

assertions.text: Rejects the DAG pattern as overkill for this case
Recommends a sequential pipeline or equivalent simple pattern instead

evals.prompt: I wrote a bash script that loops forever, invoking a coding agent each iteration to keep 'improving' a codebase, with no maximum iteration count, no cost limit, no time limit, and no way for the agent to signal it's done. Is this a safe way to run an autonomous loop? What's missing and why does it matter?
evals.expected_output: Flags the lack of any exit condition as a serious risk and recommends adding a stop mechanism such as a max iteration count, cost ceiling, time box, or completion signal before running the loop unattended.

assertions.text: Flags the missing exit/stop condition as the core problem

evals.prompt: I told my coding agent's implementation prompt: 'Write tests, but don't test framework internals, don't add excessive error handling, and don't write pointless assertions.' Now it's being oddly hesitant and skipping legitimate edge-case tests too. What went wrong and what should I do instead in my autonomous pipeline?
evals.expected_output: Explains that negative instructions bleed into unrelated judgment and cause the model to under-test broadly, and recommends letting the implementer be thorough while adding a separate de-sloppify/cleanup pass in its own context afterward.

assertions.text: Identifies negative instructions as the cause of the over-hesitancy
Recommends a separate cleanup pass instead of constraining the implementer
